key_insight: Cross-cohort breast cancer subtype accuracy is distorted by incompatible label sets, making label-space alignment essential before attributing performance differences to model skill.
clinical_relevance: Reliable subtype evaluation matters because subtype boundaries can affect treatment interpretation, but this study does not establish improved treatment outcomes.
method: Transfer a METABRIC-trained subtype classifier to TCGA-BRCA and GSE21653.
Separate label-space restriction from optional EM prior calibration.
Evaluate multimodal transfer, response prediction, and survival discrimination.
evidence_signal: Restricting predictions to each target cohort’s allowed labels raised accuracy from 73.76% to 79.74% in TCGA-BRCA (n=987) and from 63.16% to 68.42% in GSE21653 (n=266), without retraining.
watch_item: Allowed labels must come from cohort documentation, not unlabelled predictions; optional EM calibration improved Brier performance but reduced macro F1.
paper_title: Label-Space Mismatch Distorts Cross-Cohort Evaluation in Breast Cancer Molecular Subtyping
